title: Bhrigu's second answer
hookLine: a son keeps bringing his father an answer, and the father keeps sending him back, past food, past breath
carry: the self lies deeper than body and breath
tomorrow: who rose out of the furrow?

lines: ONE HONEST ANSWER AT A TIME.
cards: Breath is Brahman. That's the second answer a young man named Bhrigu brings home to his father, Varuna, in the third part of the Taittiriya Upanishad. This path met him over food, his first answer.
The clue hasn't changed: Brahman is that from which beings are born, by which they live, and into which they return. Go and practice, and find out. Food fit the clue, and still he was sent out again.
Now he's back with breath. On the last day of a season of breath: the step after food, what the Upanishad says breath is, and why the son still isn't done.

teach.b: Here's how the second answer comes, in paraphrase. Bhrigu practices again, and comes to see that breath is Brahman.

teach.h: BREATH IS THE LIFE OF BEINGS
teach.b: From breath beings are born, by breath they live, into breath they return. It fits the clue.

The second part of the same Upanishad has a short verse that says why: the gods breathe along with breath, and so do people, and so do animals. Breath is the life of beings, so it's called the life of all.
While there's life, there's breath. And still Varuna says, practice again.

teach.h: FIVE SHEATHS: FOOD, BREATH, MIND, UNDERSTANDING, BLISS
teach.b: Bhrigu goes on, to mind, to understanding, and at last to bliss, and this time he isn't sent away. The same Upanishad gives the map behind his steps, and Vedanta teachers make much of it.
A person is like a set of sheaths, koshas, one inside the next. A self made of food: the body. Inside it, a self made of breath.
Inside that, mind; then understanding; and innermost, bliss. That's the teaching: you are more than your body, and more than your breath.
Many Vedanta teachers read it this way: the true self, atman, is what every layer rests on, deeper than all of them. Breath, in this tradition, is offered, tamed, watched, called the life of all.
It's a doorway, not the house. On a day when you're out of breath, the breath is a good place to start, and Varuna would say: keep going in.

how: The Taittiriya Upanishad's story of Bhrigu is studied in Vedanta as a teaching on the layers of a person, food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss, and is also chanted in Vedic recitation.

o: the very last step of Bhrigu's search
breath as Brahman, the life of all beings
a cure Varuna gives his son for sickness

p: the five sheaths of the self

s: in the Taittiriya, gods, people and animals breathe along with breath
breath is the life of beings, the verse says, so it's called the life of all.
in the Taittiriya, beings are born from breath, live by it and return into it
breath fits the father's clue, and it's one true step on the way.
the Taittiriya's verse on breath teaches a breathing technique
it names no technique and promises no cure. it points at breath as the life of beings.

games.q: Bhrigu has found that breath is Brahman, and Varuna sends him out again. what's the lesson in that?
o: breath was wrong, so forget it.
breath is true, but the self lies deeper: keep going in.
breath is the final answer, so stop there.
games.why: breath held, but the sheaths go on: mind, understanding, bliss. many Vedanta teachers read the self, atman, as deeper than every layer.

practice: Climb Bhrigu's steps slowly: notice the body, the food that built it, the weight on the seat; then the breath, coming and going on its own; then the mind, thoughts arriving and leaving; then the knowing that is aware of all of it.
Then simply rest, and let whatever ease is there be enough. If you pray, you can rest in God's presence.

wordCard.voice: The breath again. In the Taittiriya, Bhrigu finds that breath is Brahman, and his father sends him on, past breath, to look further. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: bliss, joy. in the Taittiriya, the last step of Bhrigu's search, after food, breath, mind and understanding.

carryVoice: Your line: the self lies deeper than body and breath. Tomorrow, a new season: the women of the epics, starting with Sita. Until tomorrow.
